title: Unique Substrings With Equal Digit Frequency
summary: For a given digit string s, calculate the count of distinct substrings where each digit's frequency is identical.
statement: For a given digit string s, calculate the count of distinct substrings where each digit's frequency is identical.
constraints: s contains decimal digits and substrings are contiguous and nonempty.
A substring qualifies when every digit present in it occurs the same number of times.
Count distinct substring contents, not distinct positions or frequency vectors.
hints: Equal frequencies can be checked from ten counters, but distinct content also needs exact identity.
Build a digit trie for all substrings; the path uniquely identifies content without copying every substring.
For each start extend rightward, update one count and one trie edge, and mark an unmarked node when all positive counts match.
Each distinct substring maps to exactly one trie node. The marker counts it once, and the counter condition is exactly the equal-frequency rule.
editorial: Each distinct substring maps to exactly one trie node. The marker counts it once, and the counter condition is exactly the equal-frequency rule.
